brand.purpose: The plain-text 'L4L0' mark in the rail; the only branded, colored, monospace UI label.

body.purpose: Agent narration, opening prompt, message bubble text.

log.purpose: Raw tool-output content inside .log-block, coalesced per contiguous run.

shadows.name: composer-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system; lifts the pinned composer bar off the thread.

motion.name: line-fresh
motion.purpose: New log lines fade in inside a growing .log-block; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.note: Rail collapses to a horizontal wrapping bar; thread height computed against a hardcoded 64px rail height. Explicitly deprioritized/unpolished per user direction ('who needs for mobile') — not a validated pattern to extend.

components.name: Composer Bar
components.description: The single input driving both scan-launch (target/mission extraction) and read-only steering; pill container carries the field chrome, the input itself is borderless.
components.html: <form class="ds-composer-bar"><input class="ds-composer-input" type="text" placeholder="Tell me what to test…" autocomplete="off" /><button type="submit" class="ds-composer-send" aria-label="Send">➤</button></form>
components.css: .ds-composer-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #1b2336; border: 1px solid #263042; border-radius: 999px; padding: 8px 8px 8px 18px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); } .ds-composer-bar:focus-within { border-color: #22c55e; } .ds-composer-input { flex: 1; background: transparent; border: none; color: #f8fafc; padding: 8px 0; font-size: 0.94rem; } .ds-composer-input::placeholder { color: #8291ab; } .ds-composer-input:focus-visible { outline: none; } .ds-composer-send { flex: none; width: 36px; height: 36px; border-radius: 50%; background: #22c55e; color: #06210f; border: none; cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Log Block
components.description: A single growing monospace readout per contiguous run of raw tool output; fresh lines fade in.

narrative.overview: The console is a chat surface wearing a developer tool's palette: one scrolling thread, one composer, no dashboard of panels and no launch form. The operator's own sentence — a target plus an objective, typed in their own words — becomes the first chat bubble, and everything the running scan does (agent status, findings, chains, raw log output) narrates back as turns from 'L4L0' in that same thread. This was a pinned override, twice over: away from a starship-terminal aesthetic toward 'clean, like ChatGPT,' and away from a two-field launch form toward 'just a prompt, like a real conversation.' The build honors both: there is no <form> with separate target/mission fields anywhere, and the terminal register survives only inside the raw-output log blocks, where it belongs (real tool output from inside the scan container), not as a decorative shell around the whole page. Density is calm, not cramped: a slim 200px rail carries identity and live counters; the thread is centered and capped at 760px so long narration stays readable. The one deliberate visual departure from a pure chat app is the raw-output block, which groups consecutive log lines into a single monospace, scrollable readout rather than one bubble per line — the volume of tool output would otherwise drown the conversation.
keyCharacteristics: One thread, one composer, no separate launch form or panel dashboard
Deep slate base with a single vivid green accent, reused for both brand and 'healthy/running' state
No logo or icon; the wordmark is doing all identity work
Severity is never color-alone: every finding pairs a colored pill with its own text label

All dynamic, potentially target-influenced content renders via textContent/template cloning only — never innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, or document.write (verified: zero occurrences on any dynamic path)

rules.name: The Severity-Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every severity pill pairs a distinct background color with its own text label rendered inside the pill — color is reinforcement, never the sole signal.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Green is the only saturated brand color in the system. Warning, caution, and danger exist solely as severity-pill fills and never appear as decorative or brand color elsewhere.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for two things only — the brand wordmark and real tool output — never used for conversational text, labels, or UI chrome, so its appearance always signals 'this came from the running tool.'

rules.name: The Tonal-Not-Cast Rule
rules.body: Depth between the rail, thread, cards, and page background is conveyed by stepping through the slate scale, not by shadow. Reach for the next tonal step before reaching for a shadow.

dos: Do render every dynamic, target- or agent-influenced value via textContent or cloned <template> content only. No innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, or document.write on any dynamic path.
Do pair every severity indicator with a visible text label; never encode severity by color alone.
Do route every new operator-facing surface (findings, chains, status, logs) through the shared 'L4L0 turn in the thread' pattern rather than inventing a separate panel or modal.
Do keep the accent (#22c55e) singular — reserve it for brand, 'connected/healthy,' and the user's own sent messages; don't introduce a second brand hue.
Do use the pill radius (999px) for anything clickable/self-contained and the soft-rectangle radii for containers, per the existing split.
donts: Don't add a second input field, a launch form, or a dashboard of panels — the single composer and single thread are the pinned, load-bearing decision for this surface, confirmed twice over user course-correction.
Don't add a logo mark or icon next to the wordmark — the identity is deliberately text-only; this is confirmed, not a placeholder awaiting an asset.
Don't treat the composer's steering mode as a full chat channel — its note must always state plainly that it is read-only and cannot record findings.

Don't carry the ≤900px mobile layout forward as a validated pattern: it computes thread height against a hardcoded rail height and was explicitly deprioritized in favor of desktop for this pass — treat mobile as unpolished, not as an example to extend.
